title: Flat models and generators
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$ and $X$
a scheme of finite type over the standing field. Every $C\in\Dctf(X,A)$ on
$X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ is represented by a bounded complex of flat constructible
$A$-sheaves. A flat constructible sheaf has a finite stratification on which
it is locally constant with finite projective $A$-module local models.
Consequently $\Dctf(X,A)$ is generated, using shifts, finite extensions and
direct summands, by sheaves $a_!L$, where $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ is locally
closed and $L$ is locally constant with finite projective local models.

*Complement (generation over a Noetherian base).* More generally, let $X$ be a
Noetherian scheme and $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring. Every object of
$\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ lies in the thick subcategory of $D(X,\Lambda)$ generated by
the objects $Rg_*j_!L$, where $U\subset X$ is a locally closed stratum of a
stratification of $X$, $j:U\hookrightarrow\overline U$ is the open immersion
into its closure, $g:\overline U\hookrightarrow X$ is the closed immersion of
the closure, and $L$ is a lisse (finite locally constant) sheaf of
$\Lambda$-modules on $U$ with flat stalks. That is, every property of objects
of $D(X,\Lambda)$ that is triangulated (contains $0$ and is stable under shifts
and under extensions in distinguished triangles), stable under retracts and
under isomorphisms, and holds for all these generators holds for every object
of $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$.

Conventions. The standing field is $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of
[def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Work with ordinary module sheaves over the
constant finite ring on the small sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site;
def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and their derived categories
[def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. In either site, $\Dctf$ means bounded
constructible cohomology and Tor amplitude in some finite interval $[a,b]$:
$H^i(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}M[0])=0$ for every module sheaf $M$ and every
$i\notin[a,b]$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude; def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude].
Constructibility and lisse sheaves use
[def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf; def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf].
Flat means that tensoring with the sheaf is exact; a finite projective module
means a direct summand of a finite free module. A Noetherian scheme means a
quasi-compact locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Stratifications
are finite partitions by locally closed subschemes
[def-constructible-stratification]. For a locally closed immersion
$a:S\hookrightarrow X$, write $a_!L=g_*j_!L$ using its factorization through
its scheme-theoretic closure $S\xrightarrow{j}\overline S\xrightarrow{g}X$;
this fixes the locally closed extension-by-zero notation. The open
extension by zero is [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] on the étale site and
[def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero] on the pro-étale site. The complement is
valid on either small site with these conventions.

proof.text: We prove the model and dévissage for a finite commutative ring $B$ and a Noetherian scheme $X$, covering both the asserted $A,X$ and the complement. In the first case $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian (a field has only the ideals $0$ and $k$), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian. A Noetherian scheme is quasi-compact by definition and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. The ring $B$ is Noetherian: each ideal is a finite set and is generated by that set. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], complements of finite subunions of any family of ambient open sets have a minimal member; adjoining any further open cannot shrink it. Thus the union is already a finite subunion. Applied to ambient opens covering a subset, this shows every subset is quasi-compact, in particular every open and every stratum. These are exactly the scheme and coefficient finiteness hypotheses needed below.

source.place: First paragraph and complement: verify the Noetherian/qcqs hypotheses; morphisms.tex Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; properties.tex Tag 01OY, lemma-locally-Noetherian-quasi-separated

proof.text: Choose integers $a\le b$ witnessing the finite Tor amplitude of the input. For $C\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proét}},B)$, the equivalence in [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] gives $C_{\mathrm{ét}}\in D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\mathrm{ét}},B)$ and an isomorphism $\nu_X^*C_{\mathrm{ét}}\cong C$. Its interval clause gives the same finite Tor interval $[a,b]$ on the étale side. For an étale input, simply take $C_{\mathrm{ét}}=C$. No assumption that $B$ is a field or a coefficient quotient $A_{E,n}$ is used.

source.place: First paragraph: comparison descent; the Noetherian-ring refinement in sec-proetale-coefficients/sk-cor-pe-finite-tor-comparison/sk-cor-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian.md

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible] to $B,X,a,b,C_{\mathrm{ét}}$. It gives a complex $P_{\mathrm{ét}}$ supported in $[a,b]$, with each term flat constructible, representing $C_{\mathrm{ét}}$. On the pro-étale site put $P^q=
u_X^*P_{\mathrm{ét}}^q$ and $d_P^q=
u_X^*d_{P_{\mathrm{ét}}}^q$. By [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], this termwise functor is exact, commutes with cohomology and preserves quasi-isomorphisms; hence $P$ represents $
u_X^*C_{\mathrm{ét}}\cong C$. The terms are flat by [lem-exc-constant-inverse-image-flat] and constructible by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-sheaf-origin]. Exactness preserves zero, so $P$ has the same finite support. On the étale site use $P=P_{\mathrm{ét}}$. This proves the flat-model assertion and supplies models for the complement.

proof.text: For any flat constructible sheaf $F$, clause 1 of [det-sf-flat-model-generation] supplies an ordered finite stratification $X=\bigsqcup_{k=1}^m S_k$ with $F|_{S_k}$ locally constant with finite projective $B$-module stalks. These are finite projective local models: a local trivialization at a point has its model isomorphic to that stalk. Clause 2 of that same statement gives a finite sequence of extensions expressing $F$ in terms of $a_{k!}(F|_{S_k})$, and asserts that these sheaves are flat constructible and belong to $\Dctf$. This proves the stratification clause and gives the sheaf dévissage on either site. We use those two explicit clauses, not a resolution or construction hidden in the cited proof.

source.place: First paragraph: ordered strata and open–closed extensions; det-sf-flat-model-generation.md clauses 1–2

proof.text: For the bounded model $P$ from step 3, put $P_{\ge q}^i=0$ for $i<q$ and $P_{\ge q}^i=P^i$ for $i\ge q$, with inherited differentials between retained terms. For each $q$, use the identity inclusion in degrees $i\ge q+1$ and zero below, and the projection which is the identity in degree $q$ and zero elsewhere. The chain-map equations hold because the target of the projection has zero differentials and the included tail starts in degree $q+1$. In each degree the sequence is either $0\to P^i\xrightarrow{1}P^i\to0$ or $0\to0\to P^q\xrightarrow{1}P^q\to0$, or all zero. Hence these maps form a degreewise split short exact sequence of complexes $0\to P_{\ge q+1}\to P_{\ge q}\to P^q[-q]\to0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] its image is a distinguished triangle. Start with $P_{\ge b+1}=0$ and induct downwards from $q=b$ to $a$: the triangle expresses $P_{\ge q}$ as an extension of the already treated tail and $P^q[-q]$. Apply the sheaf extensions from step 4, converted to triangles by the same cited lemma on degree-zero complexes. Thus $C\cong P_{\ge a}$ lies in the subcategory generated by the $a_!L$ using shifts and finitely many extensions. Clause 3 of [det-sf-flat-model-generation] supplies the reverse containment and stability under direct summands, so the generation is equality with $\Dctf$. This argument uses the terms of $P$, not its cohomology sheaves. In the completed etale property clause, this bounded-complex induction is implemented by HomotopyCategory.mem_subcategory_of_strictly_bounded applied to the inverse-image property under DerivedCategory.Qh. The bounds follow from the zero terms of the model, and DerivedCategory.quotientCompQhIso identifies its image with the model in the derived category.

source.place: First paragraph and complement: stupid truncation triangles; Stacks derived.tex Tag 0152, lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor, applied to the displayed degreewise split sequences

proof.text: To identify the generators in the complement, take each stratum $a_k:S_k\hookrightarrow X$ produced in step 4. For every affine open $V\subset X$, the inverse image $a_k^{-1}(V)$ is a subset of $X$, with its induced topology, so is quasi-compact by step 1. Thus $a_k$ is a quasi-compact immersion. By [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image], it is an open immersion $j_k:S_k\hookrightarrow\overline{S_k}$ into its scheme-theoretic image, whose image is dense there; the structural map $g_k:\overline{S_k}\hookrightarrow X$ is closed by [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]. Its underlying closed set is exactly the closure of $S_k$. On the étale site, [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] states exactness of the closed direct image on finite-ring module sheaves. On the pro-étale site use [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]; its quasi-compact-complement hypothesis holds since every open subset of a Noetherian scheme is quasi-compact. Consequently the last clause of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor], which applies to an exact functor between abelian categories and identifies its termwise localization with its right derived functor, gives $Rg_{k*}=g_{k*}$ on these degree-zero objects. With the locally closed extension-by-zero convention in the statement, $a_{k!}L_k=g_{k*}j_{k!}L_k\cong Rg_{k*}j_{k!}L_k$. Every $L_k$ is lisse with flat stalks, as required. The partition is the finite ordered stratification from step 4, not the possibly invalid two-piece partition into a locally closed subset and its complement. For the implemented etale property clause, flatModelEtaleExtension already uses this canonical toImage/imageι factorization, as does sfEtaleClosureGenerators. The generator witness uses j = a.toImage and the identity isomorphism, so no additional exact-versus-derived comparison lemma is needed in that Lean proof. Finite projective stalks provide finite stalks and hence IsFiniteLocallyConstantSheaf; flatness of the restriction follows directly from Etale.upperStar preserving flat objects.

source.place: Complement: generators through their closures; Stacks morphisms.tex Tag 01QV, lemma-factor-quasi-compact-immersion, etale-cohomology.tex Tag 095L (open–closed sequence), proetale.tex Tag 09BM (exact closed direct image with retrocompact complement); derived.tex Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor

proof.text: Let $\mathcal P$ be a property as in the complement and $K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$. Use steps 1–6 with $B=\Lambda$. On every flat term of its bounded model, the finite filtration in step 4 has successive factors identified in step 6 with the assumed generators; $\mathcal P(0)$ and extension closure prove $\mathcal P$ for that term by induction on the number of factors. Shift stability gives $\mathcal P(P^q[-q])$, and the downward induction of step 5 gives $\mathcal P(P)$ and then $\mathcal P(K)$ by isomorphism stability. Closure under retracts additionally gives the stated thick-subcategory formulation. The empty scheme and zero complex use only the base case $0$, and an interval of length zero uses just one term.

source.place: Complement: final finite induction on the sheaf filtration and stupid tails

Made definitions explicit, replaced obsolete missing ids and broad section tags by precise node citations, and repaired the complement partition. All original mathematical clauses are retained. Maintainer reader: supplied the structured tool-use declarations already justified in the report; no mathematical statement, proof step or dependency changed.
split_report.blueprint: Steps 1–3 realize paragraph 1 comparison and bounded flat constructible model, also for the Noetherian complement. Step 4 realizes ordered flat sheaf strata and open–closed dévissage through the existing detailed node. Step 5 gives the stupid-tail induction; steps 6–7 realize the complement generators and property formulation. The cautionary paragraphs about cohomology and constant coefficients are recorded in the report, not used as proof premises.

tool_uses.why: The current blueprint explicitly descends along comparison; this existing theorem supplies the general finite-ring equivalence and interval preservation, not an identification with non-finite condensed coefficients.
The bounded flat constructible model is precisely the current blueprint model input; its general finite-ring statement avoids the older coefficient-restricted unit interface.
Exact comparison inverse image carries the termwise model and its quasi-isomorphism to the pro-etale site; this is a generic site-comparison tool.
Flatness preservation is a separate generic constant-coefficient inverse-image theorem; exactness alone is not used to infer it.
Finite-ring constructible sheaf comparison separately preserves constructibility of each model term.
The generic factorization of a quasi-compact immersion identifies each stratum as open in its scheme-theoretic closure.
Only its exact closed direct-image assertion is used on the etale site in the closure-generator identification.
Its exact closed direct image applies on the pro-etale site after the Noetherian retrocompact-complement check.
The generic exact-functor theorem identifies the termwise closed pushforward with its right derived functor, without additional resolution hypotheses.
